full_judgment:
8. Further case of the defendant's is that the suit is barred by limitation and, as such„ the suit is liable to be dismissed 

 16. He further submits that concurrent finding of facts based on evidence does not calls for any interference. He further submits that the plaintiff filed the suit just after his knowledge while he gone through the RS record prepared at the behest of the step-brother and filed the suit and, as such, the suit is not barred by limitation and both the Courts below considered and found that the suit is not barred by limitation. He further submits that the alleged wasiatnama has never seen the light of the sun and the defendants who obtained the properties by alleged wasiatnama failed to produce the original of the said wasiatnama and thus the alleged wasiatnama has not been proved in accordance with law and it has not been acted upon and that the defendants cannot claim the properties by dint of said wasiatnama. He further submits that evidence of DW 1 does not tally with the certified copy produced before the Court and no explanation was given by the defendants for non-production of the original deed and, as such, both the Courts below concurrently found that the alleged wasiatnama is void, illegal and not binding upon the plaintiffs. In support of his contention, he cited the case of Paresh Chandra Bhowmick vs Hiralal Nath reported in 36 DLR (AD) 156, the case of Hazi Waziullah alias Waziullah Minh vs Additional Deputy Commissioner, Revenue, Noakhali and Assistant Custodian of Vested and Non-Resident Property in 41 DLR (AD) 97, the case of Yasin Imambhai Shaikh vs Hajarabi reported in AIR 1986 (Born) 357, case of Kunhi Abulla vs Kunhi Abulla reported in AIR 1964 (Kerala) 200.
